messages:
samir: Heads-up: scan found a high-severity vuln affecting OpenSSL in our ubuntu:22.04 base image and a glibc panic workaround in a few runtime images. CVE-2026-1420. Looks like a patch exists upstream but it's not in the distro container yet. :warning:
lee: Can you paste the scanner output? which packages and versions?
samir: here's the relevant lines from snyk/clair output:
```
CVE-2026-1420 - openssl 3.0.2-1ubuntu1 - Remote certificate parsing flaw -> exploitability: network
Affected images: docker.io/redwood/base:ubuntu-22.04, docker.io/redwood/runtime/python39:2026-02-08
Fix: openssl upstream patch v3.0.6; ubuntu backport pending in focal/22.04 security repo
```
anya: :eyes: Is alpine affected? we still have some edge/alpine-based minimal images for functions.
maria: Alpine uses openssl from community/musl stack; current scan didn't flag alpine main, but we should validate musl-based images separately.
security-bot: Automated note: prioritization score 8/10 based on exposed surface and deploy count. Recommended action: patch/backport + rebuild + sign images.
samir: Proposals: (A) Wait for distro backport and rebuild ubuntu images (minimal change) OR (B) vendor a patched openssl in our CI and rebuild now (faster, more effort to maintain). Thoughts?
lee: For internet-facing services we should not wait. Option B + staged rollouts for infra tier 1. Option A ok for internal-only images.
anya: Agree with lee. Also we need to add a canary gating check in deploy pipeline: block non-signed images and require vulnerability scan pass.
maria: Implementation notes: 1) build new base image tag: ubuntu-22.04-sslpatch-2026-1420 2) run unit + smoke tests on canary cluster 3) promote after 24h metrics pass. 4) sign with cosign -> use KMS-backed key (we have KMS HSM key alias projects/redwood/cosign-key).
samir: On KMS: need to confirm the key permissions and RBAC change. Who can sign images? currently only ci-service-account. We should add a small RBAC group for "image-signing" and require 2 approvers for manual promotions.
lee: I'll open a small RBAC PR to add group and require iam:signBlob on KMS for ci-service-account and ops-sre@redwood. Also add a condition to require request from CI repo.
anya: Testing: include a quick reproducer script in the PR that pulls the new image and runs `openssl s_server -cert ...` to exercise handshake paths.
maria: Ops checklist (short):
- [ ] Build patched base images (ubuntu + runtime layers)
- [ ] Run vuln scan and integration tests
- [ ] Deploy to canary subset (10% traffic)
- [ ] Monitor latency/error budget for 12-24h
- [ ] Promote and notify customers if required
- [ ] Rotate cosign key if we had to expose it during CI changes

samir: Assigning owners: lee -> RBAC + KMS perms; anya -> CI build pipeline + canary gating; maria -> rollout plan + smoke tests; I'll coordinate the vuln triage doc and PR templates.
lee: ETA? I can do RBAC PR today, target merge by EOD tomorrow.
anya: CI changes need a little more time, target on-call window Tuesday.
maria: I'll schedule a short incident-style dry run with oncall to exercise rollback steps.
security-bot: Follow-up recommended: add a postmortem entry if any customer-facing incident occurs and record time-to-patch.
samir: Great. I'll create the GH issue and link the vuln tracker. I'll also post an update to #incidents if we decide to escalate. :+1:
ops-bot: Deploy bot: scheduled canary window available Tue 04:00-06:00 UTC.
lee: OK, I'll start RBAC PR and ping @anya when ready.
anya: Thanks all, will draft the CI changes and share later today.
maria: Leaving this thread open until we have green from canary or clear downgrade path.
samir: Closing notes: we prioritize internet-facing services first, then internal runtimes. If distro pushes backport in <48h we can consider aligning with distro patch to reduce maintenance.
